Research of 2026-11-16: CAPTIVA (University of Florida lead; collaborators NINDS, University of Cincinnati, MUSC, Janssen Scientific Affairs and AstraZeneca) randomises about 1,683 adults with a stroke in the past 30 days 'attributed to 70-99% stenosis (or flow gap on MRA) of a major intracranial artery' to ticagrelor plus aspirin (EXPERIMENTAL) or rivaroxaban 2.5 mg twice daily plus aspirin (EXPERIMENTAL), each against clopidogrel plus aspirin (ACTIVE_COMPARATOR), with efficacy primary outcome 'Number of participants with ischemic stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage or vascular death' up to 12 months (registry, clinicaltrials.gov API v2, checked 2026-11-16). The registry files 'Intracranial Arteriosclerosis' and 'Stroke' as two conditions and the asset holds both, so the readout links to neither. They are one population: the qualifying stroke is the event and intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis is the disease that selects the patients. The pair is Intracranial Arteriosclerosis (D002537). The Brilinta label (api.fda.gov set id f7b3f443-e83d-4bf2-0e96-023448fed9a8, effective 2026-05-07) covers stroke risk reduction 'in patients with acute ischemic stroke (NIH Stroke Scale score <=5) or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA)' for up to 30 days. It does not name intracranial stenosis or 12 months of treatment, so the row reads as an unapproved expansion.

RENAL LIFECYCLE (University Medical Center Groningen lead; collaborators AstraZeneca and the Dutch Kidney Foundation) randomises about 1,750 adults to dapagliflozin 10 mg/day (EXPERIMENTAL) or placebo. The population is 'advanced CKD i.e. an eGFR <=25 mL/min/1.73m2', dialysis patients and kidney transplant recipients with eGFR <=45. The primary outcome is the composite 'all-cause mortality, kidney failure, and hospitalization for heart failure' (registry, checked 2026-11-16). The registry files five conditions: Kidney Disease, Chronic; Renal Transplant Failure; Heart Failure; Kidney Failure; Death. Three of them are components of the endpoint and one is a subgroup of the same randomised population, so this is not a basket. The disease is Renal Insufficiency, Chronic (D051436). CKD is on the Farxiga label (set id 72ad22ae-efe6-4cd6-a302-98aaee423d69, effective 2026-06-03), so the row reads as already approved. However, the label says 'Initiation with FARXIGA is not recommended in patients with an eGFR less than 25' and 'Efficacy and safety trials with FARXIGA did not enroll patients with an eGFR less than 25 mL/min/1.73 m2 or on dialysis'.

Sightspire is a single-arm, open-label Phase IIIb (Hoffmann-La Roche lead, Genentech collaborator, about 250 participants) of the Port Delivery System with ranibizumab ('Device: Susvimo PDS Implant', 100 mg/mL) on a 36-week refill-exchange regimen. It enrols adults diagnosed with nAMD in the past 24 months after at least 3 anti-VEGF intravitreal injections with a demonstrated response. The primary outcome is change from baseline in BCVA averaged over Weeks 68 and 72 (registry, checked 2026-11-16). There is one condition, 'Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration', with no MeSH indexing. The pair is Wet Macular Degeneration (D057135). The SUSVIMO label (set id 9c6d9e2a-9a77-4d11-b692-de87cfde3444, effective 2025-11-21) already covers nAMD in patients 'who have previously responded to at least two intravitreal injections' with refills every 24 weeks, so the row reads as already approved. The study tests a 36-week interval in nAMD.
